reverse-bafu · calibration benchmark · n=100 · seed 7

Calibration benchmark: four evidence levels

One hundred real BAFU‑2026 unit processes, each turned into a synthetic system process by computing its cumulative inventory. The fitter is then handed a candidate input list of deliberately varying quality and asked to recover the amounts. Because the processes are real, every true input and every true amount is known — so the optimiser can be scored directly, with no report and no model in the loop. The two controls without any list — ~675 frequently used datasets or all ~12,000 as candidates — are in results/benchmark/blind-n100-seed7.md and blind-all-n100-seed7.md.

100 processes · 4 evidence levels · 400 fits 1,790 elementary flows per target no impact assessment all 400 fits 18 s

The fit is the pipeline's own calibrate step. One row per elementary flow, weighted by 1/max(|target|,|model|) so a kilogram of CO₂ and a microgram of a trace metal weigh the same, and by 1/√(flows in the group), so every (unit, compartment) group — land use, water, radioactivity, each emission compartment — contributes its mean squared relative error and counts equally. Round-off flows get weight 0. Columns and right-hand side scaled; NNLS when unbounded, BVLS when bounded. An input counts as material when its true contribution reaches 1 % of the target amount of some determined flow (round-off flows are left out, as in the flow score), and as chosen when its fitted contribution does — so structure is judged by the inventory, not by coefficient size.
